title: Throughput-to-Latency Surface Prober for Continuous Batch/Queue Dynamics
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Create a reproducible prober that maps offered throughput to latency percentiles under continuous batching + queueing for mixed client profiles. The goal is a dense surface (tokens/sec x mix skew) that surfaces p95/p99 knee points, batch-size distributions, and regression signals for runtime changes.
background: Existing harnesses cover stratified arrivals and mixed loads, but we need a compact, repeatable surface probe that combines: continuous batching dynamics, queueing backpressure, multi-class client mixes, and KV-cache warmup effects. This work will standardize how we exercise the runtime when validating kernel/quantization or scheduling changes.
goals: 1) Define a canonical sweep that produces an empirical throughput-to-latency surface (tokens/sec vs p50/p95/p99). 2) Capture secondary signals: observed batch-size distribution, queue length, effective KV cache hit rate. 3) Integrate regression detection (changepoints + alerting) into existing CI bench jobs.
approach: We will generate workload arrivals using a session-aware generator (session lengths, tokens per request) and a mix controller that composes 3 client classes: short-chat (avg 40 tokens), long-infer (avg 1024 tokens), and embedding-like (avg 64 tokens). For each mix skew and offered token/sec target we run the runtime cluster for a 10-minute steady window and collect token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, batch sizes, queue depth, and KV cache hit rate. Post-process into a grid/heatmap and apply a statistical changepoint detector across builds.
harness_design:
- Controller service that orchestrates sweeps and records metadata.
- Arrival generators implemented as lightweight Go workers to avoid client-side bottlenecks.
- Use the existing probe infra from ENG-6281 for timing primitives but with new mix controller.
- Instrumentation hooks: route-level tracing, exporter metrics (prometheus), and token counters at ingress/egress.
- Output: CSV per run + canonical JSON manifest for ingestion into/console dashboards.
metrics: tokens_offered_per_sec, tokens_served_per_sec, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, observed_batch_size_mean, observed_batch_size_p95, queue_length_mean, kv_cache_hit_rate, error_rate
config_matrix:
- offered_load: [5k, 10k, 25k, 50k, 100k, 200k, 400k] tokens/sec
- mix_skew: [balanced, short-heavy, long-heavy, embedding-heavy] (defines % per client class)
- concurrency_profile: [session_count per class: low/med/high] mapped to overall QPS
- model_variant: [gpt-like-1.0, gpt-like-1.0-quant, gpt-like-1.1]
- kv_cache_state: [cold, warm]
- runtime_flags: [continuous_batching_on/off, adaptive_scheduler_on/off]
experiment_plan: 1) Implement mix controller and arrival generator (week 1). 2) Add instrumentation for batch-size distribution and KV cache metrics (week 1-2). 3) Run smoke sweep on staging cluster to validate no client-side saturation (week 2). 4) Full grid sweep (week 3) with repeated seeds (3 runs per cell) to assess variance. 5) Post-process and add changepoint/regression gates into bench CI (week 4).
analysis_pipeline: 1) Normalize tokens_served / offered to compute effective drop/backpressure. 2) Compute percentile latencies using streaming p2 estimator. 3) Generate heatmaps (tokens/sec x mix) for p95 and observed_batch_size_p95. 4) Run changepoint detection across historical builds and flag regressions where p95 shifts > 15% with statistical significance. 5) Upload artifacts to bench dashboard and attach short-run diffs into the PR.
expected_outcomes:
- A clear throughput-to-p95 surface with identified knee points for each mix.
- Rules for acceptable regressions (e.g., p95 increase <10% within same release vs baseline).
- Integration test in bench CI that fails on large regressions and produces an artifact bundle for investigation.
results_summary: (placeholder) initial smoke runs completed: short-heavy mix shows earlier p95 knee at ~70k tokens/sec compared to balanced (~120k). Observed batch-size mean increased from 8->18 across the knee. Full-grid runs scheduled.
risks_mitigations:
- Risk: Client generator becomes the bottleneck. Mitigation: run client generators on separate machines and validate CPU/network headroom.
- Risk: KV-cache warming dominates variance. Mitigation: include cold/warm states and report warmup trajectory.
- Risk: Flaky CI due to infra noise. Mitigation: require 3 seeds per cell and use trimmed-mean for reporting.
next_steps: 1) Finish arrival-generator PR and get review from runtime infra. 2) Add exporter metrics for batch-size and queue-length. 3) Run full-grid on dedicated staging cluster and collect artifacts. 4) Draft CONOPS and runbook for investigating bench failures.
